description: I am an Astronomy graduate from Al-Azhar University with experience in astrophysics, scientific programming (Python), data analysis, and web development. My interests include space exploration, astronomical simulations, and NASA data visualization. I aim to build an innovative, scientifically accurate, and accessible project. I welcome teammates skilled in UI/UX design, JavaScript, Python, data science, and 3D visualization.
summary: Spherexplore is a web tool for exploring and comparing SPHEREx observations of five astronomical targets. We built a Python pipeline that downloads data from IRSA, cleans and aligns the image cutouts, groups observations by visit and detector, and compares images taken at the same infrared wavelength. This helps users distinguish real motion or brightness changes from differences caused by observing in different colours. The single-page website includes an interactive sky map, target selection, a timeline for choosing visits, blink and difference views, and a spectrum chart. For Barnard’s Star, our analysis measured about 10.07 arcseconds of northward motion, close to the 10.21 arcseconds predicted from catalogue data. The project makes SPHEREx data easier to explore and demonstrates how consistent image comparisons can help identify changing or moving objects.
